title: Warm Silky Middle Eastern Wheat Harees
description: A traditional Middle Eastern dish made with wheat, meat, and spices, featuring a sweet and herbal flavor profile from palm sugar and a blend of aromatic herbs, this harees recipe is a crowd-pleaser and kosher-friendly.
instructions: Rinse the wheat berries and soak them in water for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Drain and rinse the wheat berries, then transfer them to a large pot with 4 cups of water.
Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 hour, or until the wheat is tender.
In a large pan, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat, then add the chopped onion and cook until it is softened.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the lamb or beef to the pan and cook until it is browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Stir in the cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the palm sugar to the pan and cook, stirring constantly, until it is dissolved and the mixture is well combined.
To assemble the harees, combine the cooked wheat and meat mixture in a large serving dish, and serve hot.
Garnish with chopped fresh herbs, such as parsley or cilantro, if desired.
